test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is an informal group consisting of 4 to 10 individuals who seek loans against mutual guarantee?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Joint Liability Group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Joint Liability Group (JLG) is an informal group of 4-10 individuals who come together to avail loans on the basis of mutual guarantee.
 
• The concept of JLGs was introduced to provide financial support to small and marginal farmers, tenant farmers, and others with limited access to formal credit.
 
• Each member of the JLG is jointly liable for the repayment of loans taken by the group, ensuring mutual accountability.
 
• This model is widely used in rural and agricultural financing, especially in developing countries like India.
 
• JLGs are promoted by financial institutions, particularly NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development), to enhance financial inclusion in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs):**

 
 
• SHGs are informal groups of 10-20 individuals, typically women, who save money and provide small loans to members from their collective savings.
 
• Unlike JLGs, SHGs focus more on savings and empowerment rather than solely on borrowing.
 
 
 
• **Grameen Model Bank:**
 
 
• This microfinance model, pioneered by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, was first implemented in Bangladesh.
 
• It focuses on providing small loans without collateral to impoverished individuals, especially women.
 
 
 
• **Rural Cooperatives:**
 
 
• These are member-owned financial institutions that provide credit and other financial services to agricultural and rural communities.
 
• Unlike JLGs, rural cooperatives operate on a larger scale and are formally registered entities.
 
 
 
• **NABARD's Role in JLGs:**
 
 
• NABARD promotes the formation of JLGs to address the lack of formal credit for small and marginal farmers.
 
• It provides financial assistance to banks for lending to JLGs and facilitates capacity building for members.
